en.p: In the coordinate plane there are a curve $\left|y^{2}-1\right|=\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}$ and four points $\mathrm{A}(0,\,c+1)$, $\mathrm{B}(0,\,-c-1)$, $\mathrm{C}(c,\,0)$, $\mathrm{D}(-c,\,0)$. For every point $\mathrm{P}$ on the curve whose $y$-coordinate has absolute value at most 1, $\overline{\mathrm{PC}}+\overline{\mathrm{PD}}=\sqrt{5}$. When a point $\mathrm{Q}$ on the curve lies in the first quadrant and $\overline{\mathrm{AQ}}=10$, find the perimeter of triangle $\mathrm{ABQ}$. (Here $a$ and $c$ are positive.) [4 points]
